title: States Weekly: November 11, 2026
gist: CSIS India States Weekly roundup of Indian state policy moves: West Bengal's investment subsidy of up to 120% of fixed capital, Haryana's 50/50 land pooling split, Telangana's open-access power surcharge to protect DISCOMs, Delhi's 500,000-family slum rehousing plan, and a wave of ~3% DA hikes across states.

insights.claim: West Bengal's Investment Promotion Policy 2026 offers assistance worth up to 120 percent of eligible fixed capital investment in plant and machinery, paid out over up to ten years from the start of production.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: Subsidy exceeding 100% of capex signals intensifying inter-state bidding for manufacturing; relevant for site selection and India supply-chain plays.
insights.quote: it offers assistance worth up to 120 percent of eligible fixed capital investment in plant and machinery
insights.locator: West Bengal unveils a new West Bengal

insights.claim: Odisha's Dakshyata Vikas Yojana skill scheme has an outlay of $47.8 million (INR 450 crore) over FY2026-27 to FY2028-29 and targets training about 420,000 young people, including in AI, cloud computing and cybersecurity.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: Roughly $114 per trainee indicates short-course scale; signals states building labor pipelines to attract tech and overseas-job flows.
insights.locator: Odisha approves the Dakshyata Vikas Yojana

insights.claim: Haryana's Land Pooling Policy 2026 gives landowners, as a group, half of a project's total saleable area, with the development agency keeping the other half, changing how the landowner share is calculated.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: A fixed 50% saleable-area share reshapes land-assembly economics for real estate and infrastructure developers in the NCR region.
insights.quote: Landowners, as a group, will receive half of the project’s total saleable area
insights.locator: Haryana approves a Land Pooling Policy

insights.claim: Punjab now allows Change of Land Use applications and new building plans to be approved together through a single window, reducing sequential permitting steps for standalone projects.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: Faster land-use approvals could lower project lead times for developers in Punjab.
insights.locator: Punjab simplifies land-changeapprovals for standalone projects

insights.claim: Telangana's electricity regulator TGERC approved an additional surcharge of INR 0.82 ($0.0087) per kWh on open-access consumers from November 1, 2026 to March 31, 2027 to recover DISCOM fixed costs from power purchase commitments.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: Raises the cost of open-access (often renewable) procurement for large industrial users, protecting DISCOM balance sheets at the expense of C&I green-power economics.

insights.claim: Maharashtra's MSEDCL launched the Abhay Yojana 2026-27 amnesty scheme for non-agricultural consumers whose supply was permanently disconnected on or before March 31, 2026 with outstanding dues.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: Amnesty schemes point to persistent receivables stress at state distribution utilities.

insights.claim: Gujarat, Haryana, Arunachal Pradesh and Punjab each raised dearness allowance for state employees and pensioners by 3 percent, while Karnataka raised it by 2.25 percent in the same week.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: Synchronized DA hikes add to state wage and pension bills, pressuring state fiscal deficits and SDL borrowing.

insights.claim: Delhi's Slum and Shanty Relocation and Rehabilitation Policy 2026 aims to provide permanent houses to nearly 500,000 families, covering around 2 million people.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: Large-scale public housing implies construction and cement demand in Delhi if executed.
insights.locator: Delhi approves a new Delhi Slum

insights.claim: Madhya Pradesh's draft wastewater policy sets treated-water reuse targets of 20 percent by 2027, 30 percent by 2030 and 50 percent by 2037 to cut freshwater demand.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: Creates a multi-year demand runway for water treatment and recycling infrastructure providers.
insights.quote: The policy sets reuse targets of 20 percent by 2027, 30 percent by 2030, and 50 percent by 2037.
insights.locator: Madhya Pradesh releases a draft State Level

insights.claim: Jammu and Kashmir's Private Universities Rules 2026 create a framework for national and international institutions with streamlined approvals but mandate 25 percent reservation for J&K domiciles in admissions and employment.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: Opens the territory to private higher-education investment, with local-hiring quotas as a cost constraint.
insights.locator: Jammu and Kashmir notifies the Private Universities
